mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,800-£4,500 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. 5FY 200hp units start around £1,800, while EP6FDTR 250hp and 270hp units range £2,200-£4,500. Used engines start from £900. Supply & fit adds £500-£1,000 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £5,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY/EP6FDTR) engine problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle (as early as 30,000 km / 18,600 miles), high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure causing hard starting and misfires (lifespan as low as 50,000 km), carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, and excessive oil consumption (1 litre per 1,000 miles reported).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 308 GTi values typically £4,000-£14,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,800-£4,500 represents a significant investment but often makes sense for well-maintained examples. For sub-£4,000 examples, a used engine from £900 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY/EP6FDTR) engine can reach 100,000-130,000 miles. However, HPFP failure can appear as early as 31,000 miles, and timing chain issues from 18,600-65,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct 0W-30 fully synthetic oil, timely timing chain replacement and HPFP monitoring are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 308 GTi 200, 250 and 270 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first-generation 308 GTi (2010-2014) uses the 5FY (EP6DTS) engine producing 200hp. The second-generation 308 GTi (2015-2017) uses the EP6FDTR engine in two states of tune: 250hp and 270hp. Both 250hp and 270hp versions share the same 1.6L architecture, but the 270hp has a higher-output calibration and more aggressive engine mapping. The 270hp version offers 0-60mph in 5.8 seconds versus 6.0 seconds for the 250hp.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine code is 5FY (EP6DTS) for 200hp models or EP6FDTR for 250hp and 270hp models. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP is the performance flagship of the 308 range, bringing hot-hatch power to the compact family car. Powered by the Prince engine family - jointly developed by PSA and BMW - the 1.6 THP features twin-scroll turbocharging, direct injection and advanced engine management. Available in 200hp, 250hp and 270hp outputs across two generations, the 308 GTi offers genuine hot-hatch performance with 0-60mph times as low as 5.8 seconds. However, its complexity and well-documented reliability issues - particularly timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure and carbon buildup - have made it a significant source of replacement enquiries for owners of the 308 GTi.

milestones.description: **2010** - First-generation 308 GTi launched with 5FY (EP6DTS) 1.6 THP 200hp, 275 Nm torque, 0-100km/h in 7.7 seconds
**2015** - Second-generation 308 GTi launched with EP6FDTR 1.6 THP 250hp (246bhp) and 270hp (268bhp) versions
**2017** - Production of 308 GTi ends; successor models adopt electrified powertrains

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 5FY and EP6FDTR engine fitted to the Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY/EP6FDTR) is a thrilling hot-hatch engine, but its Prince architecture - shared with BMW and Mini - has well-documented weaknesses. Timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure, carbon buildup and oil consumption are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The EP6FDTR 270hp variant is particularly susceptible to timing chain and HPFP issues due to higher cylinder pressures and temperatures. Every rebuilt Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP Engines Rattle and Fail
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. The timing chain can require intervention as frequently as every 30,000 km (18,600 miles). One owner reported timing chain replacement at 58,000 miles and again at 98,000 miles. Cold-start rattle lasting 2-3 seconds indicates tensioner failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure; some owners report needing replacement twice

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage; replacement engine often the easiest and cheapest option

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle - it will sound worse than a diesel - address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option. Regular oil changes with fully synthetic 0W-30 oil are critical to preventing timing chain guide wear.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 5FY/EP6FDTR Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP Engines Fail to Start and Run Roughly
problems.rootCause: The Bosch HPFP's internal cam follower wears prematurely, causing metal contamination to circulate through the high-pressure fuel rail and injectors. Symptoms include hard starting, rough idle, misfires and, in severe cases, complete non-start. The HPFP has a reported lifespan as low as 50,000 km (31,000 miles). Early-series engines (pre-2011) are most affected. Fault codes P000A and P000B (VVT system) can also be related.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, flush fuel lines, replace inline filter
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before metal debris reaches injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full rebuild with upgraded HPFP and cleaned rail, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Essential when metallic particles have contaminated the combustion chambers

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP is catastrophic if delayed. If diagnostic codes show fuel rail pressure deviation alongside metallic fuel, budget for a full engine replacement immediately - repairing injectors alone will not prevent repeat failure. The 270hp EP6FDTR variant is especially susceptible; HPFP failure is one of the most common reasons for 308 GTi engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Find specialist Peugeot 308 GTi 1.6 THP rebuilt engines with upgraded HPFP

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup & Oil Consumption - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption. The 1.6 THP is also known for high oil consumption - one owner reported needing 1 litre of oil every 1,000 miles, which was described as "apparently normal".

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix. Monitor oil consumption closely - if it exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 miles, have the engine inspected.
